column1: # evaluator-worst.tsv - the shape of the evaluator-worst fixture, which cg_driver builds into a floor
# program and a context program (the same shape in each) and cachegrind-gate.sh measures.
# The fixture must attain the instruction maximum over every feasible count vector under the program
# limits, for the solved constants of the toolchain measuring it (gate/cost-model.py `worst`), and the
# maximum is a property of the toolchain: against one evaluator, gcc's is an or-chain (an `or` link costs
# it one instruction more than an `and`) and clang's an and-chain. So there is one row per architecture
# and compiler, and each driver builds the row its own build matches. When a row does not attain its
# toolchain's maximum the gate fails and prints the row that does; the fix is that one line, never a
# looser check. `flip` says which operands take the nots first (T: those the chain needs TRUE, F: those
# it needs FALSE), which decides how many atoms run TRUE and how many FALSE where a kind's two outcomes
# The aarch64 rows are the enumeration's answer against the evaluator as measured for this commit; the
# x86_64 rows are the same until an x86_64 run prints its own.
